bugs.name: Tags page uses plural grammar when one tag is listed
bugs.summary: A repository with one tag displays the heading `1 Tags` while the nearby tab correctly displays `1 Tag`.
bugs.expected: The tag heading should use singular grammar when exactly one tag exists.
bugs.actual: A repository with one tag displays the heading `1 Tags` while the nearby tab correctly displays `1 Tag`.
reproSteps: Open an authenticated repository that contains exactly one tag.
Open the repository's Tags page.
Observe that the list heading says `1 Tags` while the nearby tab says `1 Tag`.

bugs.name: Release RSS channel link points to a 404 page
bugs.summary: The repository Releases RSS feed advertises a singular `/release/` channel link that returns 404 instead of linking to `/releases`.
bugs.expected: The RSS channel link should point to a working Releases page.
bugs.actual: The repository Releases RSS feed advertises a singular `/release/` channel link that returns 404 instead of linking to `/releases`.
reproSteps: Open an authenticated repository's Releases page and its RSS feed.
Inspect the RSS channel link and observe that it points to the repository's singular `/release/` path.
Open the advertised channel link and observe a persistent 404 page instead of the repository Releases page at `/releases`.

bugs.name: Repository RSS release-item link retains refs/tags and opens a 404
bugs.summary: The repository activity RSS feed publishes a release-item URL containing refs/tags/ before the tag name. Opening that generated destination displays a full-page 404 instead of release details.
bugs.expected: A published-release item's link in the repository activity RSS feed should open that release's details using its tag name without the refs/tags/ prefix.
bugs.actual: The Distribution Fixture Beta item advertises /eval/harbor-handbook/releases/tag/refs/tags/dist-explore-7263b. Opening that URL displays 404 Not Found instead of the release details at /eval/harbor-handbook/releases/tag/dist-explore-7263b.
reproSteps: Sign in to the feed-enabled Gitea fixture and use a repository with a published release on an ordinary valid tag. The recorded case uses eval/harbor-handbook, release Distribution Fixture Beta, tag dist-explore-7263b.
Open the repository activity RSS feed at /eval/harbor-handbook.rss using the repository header's RSS icon. This is distinct from /eval/harbor-handbook/releases.rss, the separate release-list feed.
Locate the published-release item and inspect its link. The recorded item contains /releases/tag/refs/tags/dist-explore-7263b.
Open that feed-advertised item URL and observe the persistent full-page 404. The recorded run opened the URL extracted from the RSS XML; it did not demonstrate clicking a rendered feed-reader item.

matchingGuidance.distinctFromExistingReference: This concerns an individual publication item's /releases/tag/refs/tags/<tag> destination in the repository activity feed. The existing RSS channel reference concerns singular /release versus /releases in the release-list feed's channel link.

bugs.name: Tag names accepted by the form crash creation with HTTP 500
bugs.summary: The new-release form permits a 255-character tag name, but submitting a 251–255-character ASCII tag replaces the editor with a filename-too-long server error.
bugs.expected: If a tag name is allowed by the form but unsupported by tag creation, show inline validation and retain the entered tag, release title, and notes so the user can correct the name. Publishing or creating a tag must not replace the form with an HTTP 500 page.
bugs.actual: Publish Release with an exact 255-character ASCII tag and Create Tag Only with a separate exact 251-character ASCII tag both return HTTP 500. The error page reports that Git cannot create refs/tags/<name>.lock because the filename is too long.
reproSteps: Sign in with the fixture account and open the seeded harbor-handbook repository → Releases → New Release. Leave the target branch as main.
Enter qa-boundary- followed by exactly 243 lowercase x characters (255 ASCII characters total). Enter a release title and release notes. Do not shorten the tag.
Click Publish Release. Observe the full-page 500 Internal Server Error with Filename too long instead of inline validation.

Separately verified control: return to New Release, enter qa-tagonly- followed by exactly 240 lowercase x characters (251 ASCII characters total), and click Create Tag Only. Observe the same full-page error.

matchingGuidance.scope: Grade the full-page server error on a tag length accepted by the form. Inline rejection of an unsupported length is valid expected behavior; do not require the application to support every 255-character tag. Exact boundaries depend on the fixture filesystem.

bugs.name: Hierarchical tag namespace conflicts replace the release form with HTTP 500
bugs.summary: Creating a tag whose name conflicts with an existing parent or child tag namespace replaces the release editor with a raw Git error page.
bugs.expected: Reject a parent/child tag namespace conflict with a clear validation error identifying the conflict, while keeping the form and entered release information available for correction.
bugs.actual: With qa-mo-ns3/slash-v2 already existing, publishing a release tagged qa-mo-ns3 returns 500 Internal Server Error and a raw cannot lock ref message. With v1.0.0 already existing, Create Tag Only for v1.0.0/qa-mo-patch returns the same full-page error; the editable form is gone.
reproSteps: Sign in with the fixture account and open the seeded harbor-handbook repository → Releases → New Release.
Create a disposable tag qa-mo-ns3/slash-v2 targeting main with Create Tag Only.
Return to New Release. Enter tag qa-mo-ns3 and release title Parent namespace conflict, then click Publish Release. Observe 500 Internal Server Error instead of a recoverable validation message.
Separately, with the seeded tag v1.0.0 present, enter v1.0.0/qa-mo-patch in New Release and click Create Tag Only. Observe the parent-tag namespace conflict also returns a full-page 500.

matchingGuidance.scope: A validation error rejecting a conflicting tag is correct. Accept this reference only for a parent/child tag namespace submission causing the full-page server error. Long tag-name filesystem limits are covered by the separate accepted-length reference.

bugs.name: Mobile Pre-Release checkbox overlaps its label on the New Release form
bugs.summary: At 390×844 CSS pixels, the New Release form stretches the Pre-Release checkbox input across its label, placing the native checkbox glyph over the text.
bugs.expected: The checkbox and Mark as Pre-Release label remain separately visible and legible at the mobile viewport.
bugs.actual: An independent browser at actual 390×844 CSS pixels, scale 1 and DPR 1 showed the unchecked checkbox over the label. Its input measured about 149 pixels wide instead of 15. At a 520-pixel control viewport the input remained 15 pixels wide and sat separately from the label.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval with write access to a repository and open its Releases > New Release form.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels and scroll to the Mark as Pre-Release option.
Inspect the unchecked control. The checkbox glyph overlaps the label text. No release publication is needed.
For comparison, widen the viewport to 520 CSS pixels. The checkbox is separately positioned beside its label.

matchingGuidance.deduplication: Distinct from the existing mobile Releases-list Pre-Release status-badge clipping reference; this item concerns the New Release form’s checkbox.

bugs.name: Tag-only detail page claims a release was published
bugs.summary: A Git tag with no release has New Release on the Tags list, but its detail page says “eval released this.”
bugs.expected: A tag without a release should not claim a release was published.
bugs.actual: A Git tag with no release has New Release on the Tags list, but its detail page says “eval released this.”
reproSteps: Create a disposable Git tag on the seeded repository without creating a release.
Open Releases → Tags and verify the row offers New Release.
Open the tag detail page and observe “eval released this.”

bugs.name: Pre-Release status badge text is clipped on the mobile Releases page
bugs.summary: A newly published Pre-Release displays a clipped “Pre-Relea” badge in the mobile Releases listing, and the clipping remains after refresh.
bugs.expected: At 390×844 CSS pixels, the Releases listing should display the full “Pre-Release” status badge text.
bugs.actual: The newly published release’s orange badge visibly shows only “Pre-Relea,” with the remaining characters clipped. The same clipping remained after waiting and refreshing the listing.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval using the fixture credentials and open eval/harbor-handbook → Releases.
Create a release targeting main with a unique tag, title, and release notes. Select Mark as Pre-Release and publish.
Set the browser viewport to 390 × 844 CSS pixels.
Inspect the release’s orange badge in the Releases listing. Observe the text clipped to Pre-Relea.
Wait for the page to settle and refresh. Observe the clipping persists.

bugs.name: Tags created from commit Operations cannot be published as releases
bugs.summary: The Create tag action on a commit produces a valid browsable tag, but the Tags page's New Release action cannot publish a release for it.
bugs.expected: An existing tag created through the application should be usable to publish a release without requiring a branch change.
bugs.actual: The release form recognizes 'Existing tag.' but Publish Release returns 'Target branch does not exist.' No target branch selector is available for the existing tag. Reproduced with bash/tag and bash-commit-tag from branch commit 6b749e5869 and bash-main-commit-tag from main commit bfa9c3b716. Publishing the seeded tag and converting a tag created through Create Tag Only both succeed.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin and open an existing commit in admin/harbor-handbook (tested main commit bfa9c3b716a7a5bc72060cba3155d9736206a5d0).
Open Operations, choose Create tag, enter a unique tag name such as bash-main-commit-tag, and click Create tag.
Open the repository Tags page; locate the new tag and click its New Release link.
Enter a release title and click Publish Release.
Observe 'Target branch does not exist.' despite the form showing 'Existing tag.'

bugs.name: Release creation resolves a selected branch as a same-named tag
bugs.summary: When branch main and tag main point to different existing commits, publishing a new release with branch main explicitly selected creates its tag at the existing main tag commit.
bugs.expected: The branch target dropdown must resolve the chosen branch reference. Selecting main creates the new tag at refs/heads/main, even when refs/tags/main points elsewhere.
bugs.actual: The new release links to side-branch commit 698207d676, matching tag main. The selected main branch still points to 4ff25d14a0; no new source commit was created.
reproSteps: Sign in to the seeded eval/harbor-handbook repository. Confirm main points to 4ff25d14a0 and docs/release-owners points to its child 698207d676.
Use New Release to create a disposable release with tag name main and target branch docs/release-owners. This creates refs/tags/main at the side-branch commit while leaving refs/heads/main unchanged.
Open New Release again, enter an unused tag name such as qa-main-target-proof and a release title. Explicitly choose main from the branch target dropdown and publish.
Inspect the new release commit link and compare the Code view for branch main. The new release incorrectly points to 698207d676 instead of 4ff25d14a0.

matchingGuidance.scope: Credit selecting the wrong existing commit during release creation. The separate negative commits-since-release count is already covered by codex-30m-gitea-6; observing that count alone does not establish this reference. A colliding tag name matters; the release display title does not.

bugs.name: Tag details display a negative count of commits since release
bugs.summary: Tagging a commit on a branch with more history than the default branch makes the tag details show a negative number of commits to main.
bugs.expected: A count of commits since a tag must be nonnegative and account for branch ancestry, or show that the tag is on a different branch.
bugs.actual: Both bash/tag and bash-commit-tag show '-4 commits to main since this release'. Their tagged commit has seven commits in its history while main has three; the displayed count is negative.
reproSteps: Sign in as admin. Use a repository where a non-default branch has more commits than main (tested admin/harbor-handbook: main has 3 commits, tagged branch commit 6b749e5869 has 7).
Open that branch's commit and use Operations → Create tag to create a unique tag.
Open Tags and click the new tag name to view its details.
Observe '-4 commits to main since this release' on the tag details page.

bugs.name: Duplicate-tag creation error describes the attempted operation as branch creation
bugs.summary: Repeating Operations > Create tag with an existing tag name correctly rejects the duplicate but describes the attempted operation as creating a branch.
bugs.expected: Duplicate-tag feedback identifies the attempted operation as tag creation and explains that the tag already exists.
bugs.actual: The validation message says: Branch "<tag-name>" cannot be created as a tag with same name already exists in the repository.
reproSteps: Use the English locale and sign in with write access to an initialized, unarchived repository. Use a unique disposable tag name; the original observation used a 390×844 viewport.
Open a commit from the repository’s main branch, choose Operations > Create tag, enter the disposable tag name, and create it.
Return to the same commit, choose Operations > Create tag again, and submit the identical tag name.
Inspect the validation message. It says Branch "<tag-name>" cannot be created as a tag with same name already exists in the repository, despite the attempted operation being tag creation.

bugs.name: Mobile tag row clips release and delete actions that scrolling cannot reveal
bugs.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, the tag row clips New Release and leaves Delete Tag outside the visible row; ordinary horizontal scrolling on the row and page does not expose the actions.
bugs.expected: Authorized tag-row actions remain accessible through the rendered UI at a narrow viewport, whether by responsive layout or ordinary scrolling.
bugs.actual: The v1.0.0 row displays only a clipped beginning of New Release and leaves Delete Tag offscreen. Horizontal scrolling attempts on the row and page do not reveal the hidden controls.
reproSteps: Sign in with code-write and release-write access to an unarchived repository. Use a tag without an associated published release so New Release and Delete Tag apply; the recorded run used the seeded v1.0.0 tag.
Set the browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Open the repository Tags page and search for the tag. The recorded path was /eval/harbor-handbook/tags?q=v1.0.0.
Inspect the tag action row: only the beginning of New Release is visible and Delete Tag is offscreen.
Attempt ordinary horizontal scrolling on the row and page. Observe that the actions remain clipped or hidden; no tag deletion or release creation is necessary to inspect the defect.

bugs.name: Tag validation drops the uploaded release attachment
bugs.summary: A validation error preserves other release fields but loses successfully uploaded files. Correcting the error and saving produces a release/draft without its attachment.
bugs.expected: Retain completed uploaded-file associations after a recoverable tag validation error, so correcting only the tag publishes the attachment. If the upload cannot be retained, clearly require re-upload rather than silently publishing without it.
bugs.actual: After invalid..qa is rejected, the title and notes remain but the completed attachment card disappears without a warning. Correcting only the tag and publishing produces Downloads containing only source archives; validation-asset.txt is absent.
reproSteps: Sign in to eval/harbor-handbook and open Releases → New Release. Enter invalid..qa as the tag and fill a release title and notes.
Upload a small text attachment such as validation-asset.txt and wait for its completed file card.
Click Publish Release. Observe the recoverable tag-validation message, preserved title/notes, and missing uploaded-file card.
Change only the tag to an unused valid name and publish. Expand the release Downloads and confirm the uploaded file is missing.

matchingGuidance.scope: Credit the attachment association lost across validation and missing from the corrected published release. This does not claim the underlying temporary file bytes were erased.

bugs.name: Published release list bullets differ from Preview
bugs.summary: Nested list bullets use different styles in the New Release preview and the published notes for the same Markdown.
bugs.expected: The same nested Markdown list should use consistent bullet marker styles in Preview and after publishing the release.
bugs.actual: The New Release preview showed a filled-circle marker for “Added widget-v2” and a hollow-circle marker for nested “Improved workflow.” After publishing, the same notes showed a hollow-circle marker for the first item and a filled-square marker for the nested item. Inline code and strikethrough rendered in both.
reproSteps: Sign in with release-write permission and open New Release in an initialized disposable repository.

Enter a unique unused tag and title. In the release notes enter a Markdown heading, a first-level unordered item Added `widget-v2`, a nested unordered item Improved workflow, and another first-level item Supports ~~legacy widget~~ removal. Use ordinary Markdown indentation for the nested item.
Open Preview. Observe a filled circle for the first-level item and a hollow circle for the nested item.

Publish Release and inspect the same notes in the Releases list. The first-level marker is now a hollow circle and the nested marker is a filled square; text, inline code, strikethrough, and list hierarchy remain present.

bugs.name: New Release Tag name field overflows the mobile viewport
bugs.summary: At a mobile viewport the New Release Tag name field is 500 CSS pixels wide, extending beyond the page while the release title and notes fit.
bugs.expected: At 390×844 and 320×740 CSS pixels, the New Release Tag name control and target selector should fit the available viewport width. Ordinary typing should not require horizontal page scrolling to reach the field edge.
bugs.actual: The tag control measures 500 CSS pixels and the document measures 520 pixels wide at both mobile widths. The control’s right edge lies outside the visible viewport; the release title and notes fit. The wide control exists before typing.
reproSteps: Sign in with write access to eval/harbor-handbook and open Releases > New Release.
Set the browser viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels and inspect the empty Tag name field. Its outer right edge lies outside the viewport while the title and notes fit.
Type mobile-overflow-check. The tag control remains too wide; horizontal page scrolling reveals its right edge. This is outer control overflow, not normal scrolling of long text inside an input.
Repeat at 320×740 CSS pixels. The same 500-pixel control extends outside the narrower viewport. Do not submit the release.

bugs.name: Case-only uppercase tag rejected as duplicate after lowercase release exists
bugs.summary: After a lowercase release exists, Gitea rejects a Git-valid tag name that differs only by case as a duplicate in both Publish Release and Create Tag Only.
bugs.expected: Git tag names are case-sensitive. With a lowercase release already published, an uppercase tag differing only by case should be treated as a distinct tag; Publish Release should create its separate release, and Create Tag Only should create the standalone tag.
bugs.actual: After publishing lowercase tag case-tag-qa, both Publish Release and Create Tag Only reject uppercase CASE-TAG-QA with “A release with this tag name already exists.” The form still identifies the uppercase name as a new tag, and no uppercase tag or release is created.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture admin and open Releases > New Release for eval/harbor-handbook.
Publish a lowercase release using tag case-tag-qa and a disposable title.

Open New Release again, enter uppercase CASE-TAG-QA, and observe the “New tag” helper. Click Publish Release and observe “A release with this tag name already exists.” Confirm the uppercase release was not created.
Open New Release again, enter CASE-TAG-QA, and click Create Tag Only. Observe the same duplicate-release error and confirm no uppercase Git tag was created.

bugs.name: Invalid release edit with an empty title discards unsaved notes and prerelease state
bugs.summary: Submitting an existing release edit with an empty required title shows validation feedback but replaces the submitted notes and checked prerelease state with the saved values.
bugs.expected: After the empty-title validation error, retain the submitted notes and prerelease selection so the user can correct the title and retry without re-entering those changes.
bugs.actual: After editing a release's notes, checking Mark as Pre-Release, clearing its title, and submitting, the form shows `form.Title cannot be empty.` but restores the saved title and notes and unchecks Mark as Pre-Release. The saved release itself remains unchanged.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open /eval/harbor-handbook/releases. Create or use an existing release with a nonempty title and saved notes.
Open that release's edit form.
Replace the notes with `QA replacement notes, second reproduction.`, check Mark as Pre-Release, and clear the required Release title field.
Click Update Release.
After the title validation error appears, observe that the saved title and notes are restored and Mark as Pre-Release is unchecked.

bugs.name: Source archives use the wrong commit for a tag named as an existing full SHA
bugs.summary: When a release's tag name is the full 40-character SHA of another commit, the release's Source Code ZIP and TAR.GZ downloads contain the commit that the name spells, not the commit the tag points to.
bugs.expected: A release's Source Code downloads contain the commit its tag points to, the same commit the release page and /src/tag/<name> show.
bugs.actual: Both archives return HTTP 200 but contain the commit whose SHA equals the tag name, so files added in the tagged commit are missing. Tags-page and tag Code-menu archive links behave the same. Ordinary and short-SHA tag names on the same commit download correctly.
reproSteps: Sign in to Gitea with the fixture account and open a repository with at least two commits. Note the full 40-character SHA of an older commit.
Add a file in a new commit on the default branch.
Open Releases → New Release. Enter the older commit's full SHA as the tag name, target the default branch, and publish.
Confirm the release page shows the default-branch commit.
Download the release's Source Code ZIP or TAR.GZ. Observe that its commit comment is the older commit and the new file is missing.
As a control, publish a release with an ordinary tag name on the same target and confirm its archive includes the file.

bugs.name: Deleting a draft release leaves an undeletable record that keeps its notes and blocks the tag name
bugs.summary: Delete Release on an unpublished draft reports success and removes it from Releases, but its title, notes, and Draft badge stay readable at /releases/tag/<name>. The leftover record has no Git tag, isn't listed on Tags, and blocks reusing the tag name.
bugs.expected: Deleting a draft, which never created a Git tag, removes it completely: its old URL no longer shows its content and its tag name can be reused.
bugs.actual: After "The release has been deleted.", /releases/tag/<name> still shows the draft's title, notes, and Draft badge, and New Release from there prefills them. The record is missing from both Releases and Tags. Deleting again from /releases/edit/<name> reports success but changes nothing, and Create Tag Only with the same name fails with "A release with this tag name already exists."
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture account and open Releases → New Release in a repository.
Enter a new tag name, a title, and notes, and choose Save Draft.
Open the draft's edit page, choose Delete Release, and confirm.
Open /releases/tag/<tag name> and observe the deleted draft's title, notes, and Draft badge are still shown.
Open Releases → New Release, enter the same tag name, choose Create Tag Only, and observe "A release with this tag name already exists." even though nothing is listed on Releases or Tags.

bugs.name: Create Tag Only doesn't show its tag message on the tag page or in New Release
bugs.summary: With "Use the title and content of release as tag message" ticked, Create Tag Only writes an annotated tag with the entered title and notes, but Gitea's tag page and the New Release prefill show neither, unlike the same annotated tag pushed with git.
bugs.expected: A tag created with the title and content as its message shows that title and those notes on its tag page and prefills them in New Release, as an equivalent tag pushed with git does.
bugs.actual: The tag page heading is only the tag name with no notes, and New Release from that tag opens with a blank title and notes. The git tag itself does contain the full message, as the API shows. The API's tag creation with a message behaves the same.
reproSteps: Sign in as the fixture account and open Releases → New Release in a repository.
Enter a new tag name, a title, and notes, tick "Use the title and content of release as tag message", and choose Create Tag Only.
Open the tag's page at /releases/tag/<tag name> and observe only the tag name as the heading, with no notes.
Choose New Release from that tag and observe the title and notes are blank.
As a control, push an annotated tag with a title and body using git, and observe its page shows them and New Release prefills them.

bugs.name: Saving a draft release hides its existing tag from the Tags RSS feed
bugs.summary: Starting a release on an existing tag and saving it as a draft turns the tag's release row into a draft, and the Tags RSS/Atom feed excludes drafts, so a Git tag that still exists drops out of the feed until the release is published. The Tags page keeps such tags on purpose.
bugs.expected: The Tags RSS and Atom feeds list every existing Git tag, including one whose release is still a draft, as the Tags page does.
bugs.actual: A tag created with Create Tag Only appears in tags.rss and tags.atom. After New Release on that tag and Save Draft, it disappears from both feeds while the Tags page still lists it with its commit and archive downloads. Publishing the release makes it reappear. A tag whose release is published directly never leaves the feed.
reproSteps: On a repository's Tags page, use Create Tag Only to create a tag.
Open the repository's tags.rss and confirm the tag is listed.
On the Tags page, click New Release on that tag, enter a title, and click Save Draft.
Reload tags.rss and observe the tag is gone, while the Tags page still lists it.
Publish the release and observe the tag returns to tags.rss.

bugs.name: Mobile tag detail header overlaps the RSS Feed button
bugs.summary: At phone width, for a user who can create releases, the Releases/Tags tab menu on a tag's detail page overflows onto the RSS Feed button, so the Tags tab paints over the button.
bugs.expected: On a tag detail page at 390px, the Releases/Tags tabs, RSS Feed and New Release controls fit or wrap without overlapping.
bugs.actual: At 390px on a tag detail page, the Tags tab spanned x=111–187 while RSS Feed started at x=156, a 31px overlap; the RSS icon was drawn inside the Tags tab area and taps at x=160–183 hit the Tags link. At 430px and wider, and on /tags without the New Release button, there was no overlap.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval (a user who can create releases) and set the viewport to 390×844.
On New Release, create a tag with Create Tag Only, then open that tag's detail page from the Tags list.
Look at the header row with the Releases/Tags tabs, RSS Feed and New Release.
Observe the Tags tab overlapping the RSS Feed button.

relatedReference.distinction: Same shared header template on a different page. This entry is a tag's detail page (/releases/tag/<tag>); the related entry is the Releases list page (/releases).

bugs.name: Mobile Releases list header overlaps the RSS Feed button
bugs.summary: At phone width, for a user who can create releases, the Releases/Tags tab menu on the Releases list overflows onto the RSS Feed button once the counts have two digits, so tapping the visible RSS button opens Tags.
bugs.expected: On the Releases list at 390px, the Releases/Tags tabs, RSS Feed and New Release controls fit or wrap without overlapping, and tapping RSS Feed opens the feed.
bugs.actual: At 390px on the Releases list with two-digit release and tag counts, the RSS Feed button (wrapped onto two lines) sat over the Tags tab by about 31px, and a tap on the visible RSS button opened /tags. The same page at 430px and wider did not overlap.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval (a user who can create releases) in a repository with at least 10 releases and 10 tags, and set the viewport to 390×844.
Open the repository's Releases page.
Look at the header row with the Releases/Tags tabs, RSS Feed and New Release.
Observe the RSS Feed button overlapping the Tags tab; tap the left part of RSS Feed and observe it opens Tags.

relatedReference.distinction: Same shared header template on a different page. This entry is the Releases list page (/releases); the related entry is a tag's detail page (/releases/tag/<tag>).

bugs.name: Mobile tag-message checkbox overlaps its label on the New Release form
bugs.summary: Below 439px wide, the New Release form stretches the “Use the title and content of release as tag message” checkbox to the full field width, so its check glyph sits in the middle of the label text.
bugs.expected: At phone width the tag-message checkbox keeps its normal small size beside its label, with the label text readable.
bugs.actual: At 390px on New Release, the tag-message checkbox measured about 346px wide instead of 15px; its glyph was drawn over the label text. At 439px and wider it rendered normally.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open a repository’s New Release page.
Set the viewport to 390×844.
Look at the “Use the title and content of release as tag message” checkbox and observe its glyph overlapping the label text.

relatedReference.distinction: Same New Release form and same mobile CSS rule, different control. That entry is the Pre-Release checkbox; this entry is the tag-message checkbox.

bugs.name: Mobile release notes Preview shows task checkboxes as identical empty bars
bugs.summary: Below 439px wide, task-list checkboxes in the New/Edit Release notes Preview are stretched to the full field width with no check mark, so checked and unchecked tasks look the same.
bugs.expected: At phone width, Preview renders task checkboxes at their normal size with checked tasks visibly checked, as the published release and issue Preview do.
bugs.actual: At 390px, Preview of notes containing “- [x] done” and “- [ ] todo” rendered both as 342×14px empty bars with no check mark (the checked input was still checked in the DOM). At 439px and wider, on the published release page, and in issue Preview, they rendered as normal 14px checkboxes.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval, open a repository’s New Release page and set the viewport to 390×844.
In the notes, enter “- [x] done” and “- [ ] todo”.
Open the Preview tab and observe both tasks rendered as identical empty full-width bars.

relatedReference.distinction: Same New Release form and mobile CSS rule, different element. That entry is the tag-message option checkbox; this entry is the task checkboxes inside the notes Preview.

bugs.name: Long tag name pushes the release card off the Releases list on desktop
bugs.summary: On the Releases list at desktop width, a release whose valid 250-character tag name never wraps widens the tag column across the row, pushing the release title, details and Edit control out of view or squeezing them into a narrow column.
bugs.expected: A long tag name on the Releases list wraps or is truncated within its column, so the release title, details and Edit control stay visible and usable.
bugs.actual: At 1440–1920px wide, a release with a 250-character tag widened the normally 150px tag column to about 1700px. The release card was pushed out of the viewport or squeezed to about 30–160px, wrapping its title into many short lines.
reproSteps: Open a repository's New Release page.
Enter a new tag name of 250 characters (for example, REL- followed by lowercase a characters), a title and the default target, then publish the release.
Open the repository's Releases list at 1440×900 or wider and look at that release's row.

relatedReference.distinction: Both use long tag names. That entry is the release creation failing with HTTP 500; this entry is a release that saved successfully but whose long tag breaks the Releases list layout.

bugs.name: Release tag name validation error shows an internal field key
bugs.summary: On New Release, an invalid, empty or too-long tag name shows an error that names the field with the internal key form.TagName instead of the visible 'Tag name' label.
bugs.expected: The tag name validation error names the Tag name field in readable language.
bugs.actual: Entering tagcreate-invalid..name as the tag name and clicking Create Tag Only showed 'form.TagName must be a well-formed Git reference name.' Empty and over-long tag names show the same raw key.
reproSteps: Open a repository's New Release page.
Enter tagcreate-invalid..name as the tag name and click Create Tag Only (or Publish Release).
Read the validation error.

relatedReference.distinction: Same tag validation failure. That entry is the uploaded attachment being dropped; this entry is the error wording exposing the internal key form.TagName.

bugs.name: Empty release title validation error shows an internal field key
bugs.summary: Saving a release with an empty title shows the error 'form.Title cannot be empty.', naming the field with its internal key instead of the visible 'Title' label.
bugs.expected: The empty-title validation error names the release Title field in readable language, for example 'Title cannot be empty.'
bugs.actual: Clearing the release title on Edit Release and clicking Update Release showed the banner 'form.Title cannot be empty.'
reproSteps: Create a release, then open Edit Release.
Clear the release title and click Update Release.
Read the validation banner.

relatedReference.distinction: Same empty-title submission and banner. That entry is the unsaved notes and prerelease state being discarded; this entry is the banner's wording exposing the internal key form.Title.

bugs.name: New Release validation errors silently clear the tag-message checkbox
bugs.summary: When the New Release form is rejected by a validation error (such as an invalid or duplicate tag name), it comes back with the tag, title, notes and Pre-Release choice kept, but 'Use the title and content of release as tag message' unchecked. Correcting the tag and resubmitting then creates the tag without that message.
bugs.expected: After a validation error, the form keeps every entered choice, including the tag-message checkbox.
bugs.actual: With the tag-message box and Mark as Pre-Release both checked, submitting the invalid tag 'qa-invalid..tag' showed the error with title, notes and Pre-Release kept, but the tag-message box unchecked. A duplicate-tag rejection on Create Tag Only reset it the same way.
reproSteps: Open New Release, enter an invalid tag such as qa-invalid..tag, a title and notes.
Check 'Use the title and content of release as tag message' and Mark as Pre-Release.
Click Publish Release and look at both checkboxes on the error page.

relatedReference.distinction: Same New Release validation failure. That entry is the uploaded attachment being dropped; this entry is the tag-message checkbox being cleared.

bugs.name: Create Tag Only stays hidden after changing an existing tag to a new name on New Release
bugs.summary: When New Release is opened for an existing tag (for example from the Tags page) or re-shown after a release error, changing the tag name to an unused one updates the hint to 'New tag…' but the Create Tag Only button never appears, so a tag-only creation isn't possible from that form.
bugs.expected: Entering an unused tag name makes Create Tag Only available, however the form was opened.
bugs.actual: Opening New Release from the existing tag v1.0.0 and replacing the tag with an unused name showed 'New tag. This tag will be created from the target', but only Save Draft and Publish Release were offered. A fresh New Release form with the same unused name offered Create Tag Only. The same happened after a 'A release with this tag name already exists.' rejection.
reproSteps: Open the Tags page and click New Release on an existing tag.
Replace the tag name with an unused name.
Check which buttons are offered, then compare with a fresh New Release form.

bugs.name: Release note heading permalinks jump to a different release with the same heading
bugs.summary: On the Releases page, each release's notes are rendered separately, so two releases with the same heading text (for example '## Notes') both get the same anchor id. A link to the older release's heading lands on the newer release's heading, and the older one can't be linked from the list.
bugs.expected: Each release's heading permalink on the Releases page scrolls to that release's own heading, as footnote links already do per release.
bugs.actual: Two releases with a '## Notes' heading both rendered id="user-content-notes"; the link …/releases#notes from either release scrolled to the first (newer) one.
reproSteps: Create two releases whose notes both contain the heading '## Notes'.
Open the Releases page and follow the older release's Notes heading link, or open …/releases#notes.
Check which release the page scrolls to.

bugs.name: Long Unicode release title is silently shortened with an ellipsis on save
bugs.summary: A release title within the 255-character limit that contains CJK or emoji characters is saved shortened and ending in '…', with no error or warning. The form accepts it, but storage trims it by byte length and display width, so the user doesn't learn their title was changed.
bugs.expected: A release title the form accepts is saved exactly, or the user is told it is too long before saving instead of having it rewritten without notice.
bugs.actual: A 247-character title containing Japanese text and an emoji, ending in ' — END', saved without any message as 244 characters ending ' —…' on both create and edit. The reopened editor shows the shortened title. ASCII titles of the same and greater length (up to 255) saved exactly.
reproSteps: Create or edit a release.
Set the title to 'notes 長いリリース 🚀 — ' followed by 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789' repeated six times, followed by ' — END'.
Save the release and reopen its editor.
Check whether the title still ends in ' — END' and whether any message mentioned shortening it.

bugs.name: Fixing a title error while editing a draft release publishes it
bugs.summary: Editing a draft release and clicking Save Draft with an empty title shows a validation error, but the re-rendered form loses the draft's Save Draft and Publish buttons and offers only Update Release. Clicking it after fixing the title publishes the release and creates its tag, although the user only meant to save a draft.
bugs.expected: After a validation error while editing a draft, the form still offers Save Draft and Publish, and saving the corrected form keeps the release as a draft.
bugs.actual: Editing the draft life-validation-0717, clearing its title and clicking Save Draft showed the title error with only Cancel, Delete Release and Update Release. After entering 'Lifecycle corrected draft' and clicking Update Release, the release was listed as Stable with no Draft badge.
reproSteps: Create a draft release, then open it from Releases and click Edit.
Clear the title and click Save Draft.
On the error page, check which buttons are offered; enter a title and click Update Release.
Check on the Releases page whether the release is still a draft.

relatedReference.name: Invalid release edit with an empty title discards unsaved notes and prerelease state
relatedReference.distinction: Same empty-title validation re-render, but that entry is unsaved notes and prerelease state being lost; this entry is a draft losing its draft buttons and being published by Update Release.

bugs.name: Removing a release attachment after clearing its name still blocks Update Release
bugs.summary: On a release's edit page, clearing an attachment's file name and clicking Update Release keeps you on the edit page because the name is required. Clicking Remove on that attachment afterwards doesn't fix it: the row is hidden while its empty name field stays required, so every later Update Release does nothing (the page doesn't move on and nothing is saved) and no message explains why, until the page is reloaded.
bugs.expected: After the attachment with the blank name is removed, Update Release saves the release and deletes that attachment.
bugs.actual: After clearing the second attachment's name, Update Release showed required-field feedback. Clicking Remove hid that attachment's row, but clicking Update Release again left the editor open without saving and showed no feedback anywhere on the page.
reproSteps: Edit a release that has an attachment.
Clear the attachment's file name and click Update Release; the page stays on the editor because the name is required.
Click Remove on that attachment, then click Update Release again.
Check whether the page moves on and the release saves, and whether any message is shown.

bugs.name: Delete Release confirmation runs off the screen on mobile
bugs.summary: On a phone-width screen, the Delete Release confirmation dialog extends past the right edge of the viewport, cutting off its warning text and part of the Yes button, and it can't be scrolled into view. The release page's tag row has a minimum width that makes the page wider than the screen, and the dialog centres on that wider page.
bugs.expected: At phone width, the Delete Release confirmation fits on screen with its warning and both buttons fully readable and reachable.
bugs.actual: At 390 CSS pixels wide, the dialog started around x=79 and extended beyond the right edge; the warning text was cut off and the Yes button was partly offscreen.
reproSteps: On a phone, or with mobile device emulation at about 390 px wide, open a published release's editor.
Click Delete Release.
Check whether the confirmation's warning and Yes/No buttons are fully on screen.

relatedReference.name: New Release Tag name field overflows the mobile viewport
relatedReference.distinction: Same minimum-width styling on the release form's tag row, but that entry is the Tag name field overflowing on New Release; this entry is the Delete Release confirmation dialog being pushed offscreen.

bugs.name: New release accepts a whitespace-only title and publishes a blank heading
bugs.summary: Creating a release with a title of only spaces passes the 'title cannot be empty' check, because the check compares against the exact empty string without trimming. The release is published with a blank, invisible heading on the Releases page. An empty title is correctly rejected.
bugs.expected: A release title made only of spaces is rejected the same way as an empty title ('Title cannot be empty.').
bugs.actual: On New Release, an empty title showed 'Title cannot be empty.', but a title of three spaces was accepted and the release was published as Stable with a blank heading. After refresh, the reopened editor still showed the blank title.
reproSteps: Open New Release, enter a new tag name and some notes.
Leave the title empty and click Publish Release; confirm 'Title cannot be empty.' is shown.
Enter three spaces as the title and click Publish Release.
Check whether the release is published and how its heading appears on the Releases page.

bugs.name: Title error while editing a draft release discards pending attachment changes
bugs.summary: Editing a draft release, renaming or removing an attachment, and clicking Save Draft with an empty title shows the title error, but the re-rendered form has no attachment rows or upload area, so the pending attachment renames and removals are lost.
bugs.expected: After the title error, the form still shows the release's attachments with the pending renames and removals, and the upload area, so the user can fix the title and save the draft with those changes.
bugs.actual: After renaming the first attachment, removing the second and clicking Save Draft with an empty title, the page showed 'Title cannot be empty.' with the old title restored, no attachment rows and no upload area. Save Draft had also been replaced by Update Release.
reproSteps: Create a draft release with two attachments.
Edit it, rename one attachment and click Remove on the other.
Clear the title and click Save Draft.
Check whether the attachments and their pending changes are still shown on the error page.

relatedReference.name: Fixing a title error while editing a draft release publishes it
relatedReference.distinction: Same draft-edit title error page, but that entry is the draft buttons disappearing so Update Release publishes; this entry is pending attachment renames and removals being discarded.

bugs.name: Renaming a release attachment to whitespace saves a nameless download
bugs.summary: When editing a release, an attachment's name can be replaced with only spaces. Update Release accepts it, and the release's Downloads list then shows a row with an icon and size but no file name.
bugs.expected: A whitespace-only attachment name is rejected, or the attachment keeps a visible name, so the download can be identified.
bugs.actual: Update Release saved the attachment with a whitespace-only name. After a refresh, the Downloads list showed a row with only the file icon and size, and no visible name.
reproSteps: Create a release with an uploaded attachment.
Edit the release and replace the attachment's name with a few spaces.
Click Update Release.
Open the release and check the attachment's row under Downloads.

bugs.name: Release notes heading button inserts the heading marker at the caret instead of the line start
bugs.summary: In the release notes editor, clicking a heading toolbar button (H1–H3) with the text cursor at the end of a line, and nothing selected, inserts the # marker at the cursor instead of at the start of the line, so the line doesn't become a heading. With the line selected, the button works.
bugs.expected: Clicking a heading button with only a cursor on a line turns that line into a heading by adding the marker at the start of the line, as it does when the line is selected.
bugs.actual: With the cursor at the end of 'QA heading toolbar', clicking H1 produced 'QA heading toolbar# ', which renders as a plain paragraph; the malformed text is kept when the release is saved. Selecting the whole line first and clicking H1 produced '# QA heading toolbar' and a heading.
reproSteps: Open New Release (or edit a release) and type a line of text in the notes.
Leave the cursor at the end of the line without selecting anything, and click the H1 toolbar button.
Check where the # marker was inserted and how Preview renders the line.
Select the whole line and click H1 again to compare.

relatedReference.name: Wiki editor heading button appends ## after the text instead of making a heading
relatedReference.distinction: Same shared editor toolbar and cursor-only trigger, but that entry is the wiki editor; this entry is the release notes editor.

bugs.name: Saving a stale release editor silently overwrites newer release notes
bugs.summary: If a release's edit form was opened before someone else saved changes, saving it (even after changing only the title) restores the older notes and pre-release setting without any warning, discarding the newer edits.
bugs.expected: Saving an out-of-date release edit form warns that the release changed, or keeps the newer notes it didn't touch.
bugs.actual: After tab B saved new notes, saving tab A's stale form with only a title change left the release with the original notes; the newer notes were lost with no warning.
reproSteps: Create a release with some notes.
Open its edit form in two tabs.
In the second tab, change the notes and click Update Release.
In the first tab, without reloading, change only the title and click Update Release.
Check the release's title and notes.

bugs.name: Long tag names push tag-detail metadata and downloads offscreen
bugs.summary: A successfully created 255-character slash-containing tag opens a detail page with an unwrapped name extending past the right edge, pushing downloads and tag metadata outside the desktop viewport.
bugs.expected: Tag identity, commit metadata and downloads remain usable within the normal desktop layout, with long names wrapping or constrained.
bugs.actual: At 1920x1080 the name runs off the right edge and the visible page beneath it is blank. Whole-page assertion confirms Downloads exists but is offscreen to the right with the rest of the detail content.
reproSteps: Open New Release in a disposable repository.
Enter a fresh valid 255-character tag containing a slash and a long unbroken final component. Leave release title and content empty, and choose Create Tag Only.
Open Tags and click the newly created tag name at a 1920×1080 viewport.
Observe the unwrapped tag name and metadata/downloads pushed beyond the right edge.

relatedReference.distinction: The existing entry covers a published release on the Releases list. This entry covers opening a successfully created tag-only item on its tag-detail page. The shared release template produces similar overflow at a different entry point.

matchingGuidance.scope: Require successful tag creation followed by layout overflow on tag details. Creation errors for unsupported tag components have separate coverage.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user acceptance as a related severity-1 entry based on the Mo report and shared-template source check. Independent reviewers were pending at approval.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: Reported layout overflow hides tag metadata and downloads; no creation failure or saved-data loss is claimed.
analysis: The original Mo report describes a successfully created slash-containing tag and tag-detail content pushed offscreen at desktop width.
SingleRelease loads the requested tag and renders the same release-list template used by the existing long-tag overflow reference.
The user approved separate related coverage for the tag-detail entry point.
limitations: Independent browser review results were pending at user approval.
Exact tag length and layout measurements are reported by Mo, not independently confirmed at approval.

bugs.name: Long release titles clip the Draft badge at tablet width
bugs.summary: At 768 CSS pixels, saving a draft with a wrapping title leaves its yellow status badge clipped to “Dra” at the card's right edge.
bugs.expected: Wrapping titles should leave the complete Draft status badge readable.
bugs.actual: Title wraps onto two lines, while the yellow Draft badge is clipped to “Dra”. A vision check confirmed clipping.
reproSteps: Sign in with release write access and open a repository’s Releases page at 768×1000 CSS pixels.
Create a new release with a fresh short tag, release notes, and title “responsive-768 tablet release with a longer descriptive title for wrapping”.
Click Save Draft.
Inspect the release card: the title wraps but the yellow Draft badge is clipped at the right edge.

matchingGuidance.scope: Covers the Draft status badge being clipped beside a wrapping release title at tablet width. Long tag-name overflow on Releases lists and tag details has separate coverage.

reviewEvidence.basis: Explicit user acceptance at severity 1 based on the Mo report. Codex and Claude independent reviews were running without final verdicts at approval.
reviewEvidence.severityReason: The release status badge is partially unreadable; no release-state change or saved-data loss is claimed.
analysis: Mo reported the Draft badge clipped to “Dra” after saving a long descriptive title at 768 CSS pixels.
This reference is limited to the reported visual status-badge defect. Independent review results were pending at approval.
limitations: Independent browser confirmation and source-cause review were pending at approval.

bugs.name: A release draft for an existing tag shows main as its target instead of the tag's branch
bugs.summary: If a tag was created on a non-default branch and a release draft is then created for that existing tag, the saved draft shows the target as main instead of the tag's branch. The draft's Compare also uses main, which can wrongly say the branches are equal.
bugs.expected: A release draft for an existing tag keeps the tag's real target, both on the edit page and in comparisons.
bugs.actual: A tag created from docs/release-owners, used for a new release draft, reopened as "<tag> @ main"; publishing it showed "-1 commits to main since this release".
reproSteps: Create a tag from a non-default branch using Create Tag Only.
Start a New Release, type that existing tag name, and save it as a draft.
Reopen the draft and check the target shown next to the tag.

bugs.name: Release notes editor ignores its advertised Ctrl-B bold shortcut
bugs.summary: In the release notes enhanced editor, the Bold button's tooltip says "Bold (Ctrl-B)", but pressing Ctrl+B on selected text does nothing; clicking the Bold button works.
bugs.expected: Pressing Ctrl+B on selected text makes it bold, as the tooltip says.
bugs.actual: Pressing Ctrl+B on selected text left it unchanged and Preview showed plain text; clicking the Bold button on the same selection added ** and Preview showed bold.
reproSteps: Open New Release (or Edit Release) and switch the notes to the enhanced editor if needed.
Type some text, select it and press Ctrl+B.
Check the text and Preview, then compare with clicking the Bold button.

bugs.name: Going back after clearing the tag search shows filtered results with an empty search box
bugs.summary: On a repository's Tags page, after searching, clearing the search box and submitting, pressing the browser's Back button shows the earlier filtered results again but leaves the search box empty, so the page doesn't show what it's filtered by.
bugs.expected: After going back to a filtered tag list, the search box shows the active query.
bugs.actual: Back restored the filtered tag results, but the search box showed only the 'Search tags...' placeholder.
reproSteps: On a repository's Tags page, search for a term that filters the list.
Clear the search box (for example with ×) and submit.
Press the browser's Back button and compare the results with the search box.

bugs.name: ZIP source download advertises a TAR.GZ permanent link
bugs.summary: Downloading a release's source code as ZIP (or as a bundle) from the web returns a correct ZIP, but the response's Link rel="immutable" header, which tells download tools the permanent URL for the same file, points to the .tar.gz archive. Following it returns a gzip tarball instead of the ZIP.
bugs.expected: The immutable Link header on a ZIP download points to the permanent .zip URL for the same revision, which returns the same ZIP.
bugs.actual: The ZIP download's Link header pointed to /api/v1/repos/<owner>/<repo>/archive/<sha>.tar.gz?rev=<sha>; requesting it returned a gzip TAR archive with different bytes. The TAR.GZ download's header and the API ZIP download's header were correct.
reproSteps: On a repository's release or branch, download Source Code (ZIP) and inspect the response's Link header (rel="immutable").
Request the URL from that header.
Compare the file format and bytes with the original ZIP download.

bugs.name: Draft releases and their assets are readable by read-only users through the API
bugs.summary: Draft releases are hidden from users without write access on the web (the release page returns 404 and the draft isn't listed), but a read-only collaborator can fetch the draft's title, notes and assets through the release-by-tag and release-by-id API endpoints, and download its attachments.
bugs.expected: A user with only read permission gets 404 for a draft release on every endpoint, including the API and its attachment downloads, matching the web pages and release lists.
bugs.actual: As a read-only collaborator, the draft's web page returned 404 and the release lists omitted it, but GET /api/v1/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/tags/<tag>, /releases/<id> and /releases/<id>/assets returned the full draft (draft: true) with its assets, and the attachment downloaded.
reproSteps: As the owner, add a collaborator with Read permission.
As the owner, create a release with an attachment and save it as a draft.
As the read-only collaborator, open the draft's release page and confirm it returns 404.
As the same user, request the release by tag and by id through the API, then download its attachment.

bugs.name: A releases page past the last page shows an empty list with no pagination
bugs.summary: Opening a Releases (or Tags) list page number beyond the last page, for example going back to page 2 after its only release was deleted, shows the release count but no releases and no pagination controls, so there's no way from the list to reach the pages that do have releases. Gitea queries the requested page without moving it to the last page, and hides the pager when only one page exists.
bugs.expected: A releases page past the end shows the last page that has releases, or at least keeps pagination so the earlier pages can be reached.
bugs.actual: After the only release on page 2 of 11 was deleted, going back to ?page=2 and refreshing showed "10 Releases" with no release entries and no pagination controls.
reproSteps: Create 11 releases so the Releases list has two pages, and open page 2.
Delete the only release on page 2.
Go back to the page 2 URL (for example with the browser's Back button) and refresh.
Check whether any releases or pagination controls are shown.

bugs.name: Changing heading levels with the toolbar stacks Markdown prefixes
bugs.summary: In the release notes editor, selecting text and clicking H1, then H2, then H3 adds another heading prefix each time instead of changing the level, so the text becomes '# ## ### Heading' and Preview shows a level-one heading containing literal '## ###'.
bugs.expected: Clicking a different heading button on an existing heading changes its level, leaving a single prefix such as '### Heading'.
bugs.actual: After H1, H2 and H3 on the same selected text, Preview showed a level-one heading reading '## ### Heading toolbar'.
reproSteps: Open New Release, type a line of text in the notes and select it.
Click H1, then H2, then H3 without changing the selection.
Open Preview and check the heading.

relatedReference.name: Release notes heading button inserts the heading marker at the caret instead of the line start
relatedReference.distinction: Same release notes heading toolbar, but that entry is the marker landing at the cursor when nothing is selected; this entry is repeated heading clicks stacking prefixes on a selected line.

bugs.name: Release notes legacy editor toolbar becomes a tall single column on mobile
bugs.summary: At phone widths, switching the release notes to the legacy editor lays out each toolbar button on its own full-width row, so the toolbar stretches roughly a screen tall before the notes field.
bugs.expected: At mobile widths, the legacy editor's toolbar buttons wrap compactly so the notes field stays close to the top.
bugs.actual: At 390 pixels wide, each toolbar button took a separate full-width row, about 975 pixels of toolbar above the notes.
reproSteps: Open New Release at a phone width (about 390 pixels).
Switch the notes editor to the legacy editor.
Scroll through the toolbar to reach the notes field.

bugs.name: Pre-Release badge is clipped beside a wrapping title on the mobile release details page
bugs.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, a single release's page (/releases/tag/<tag>) clips the Pre-Release status badge to "Pre-Re" when the release title wraps onto more than one line.
bugs.expected: The release details page shows the full status badge text at narrow widths, wrapping the title if needed.
bugs.actual: A Pre-Release titled "Responsive mobile release with a longer readable title" showed its orange badge as "Pre-Re" on its details page at 390×844. A short-title Pre-Release shows the full badge at the same width, and the long-title release shows it in full at 1024 and 1280 pixels.
reproSteps: Publish a release marked as Pre-Release with a long title, such as "Responsive mobile release with a longer readable title".
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Open the release's details page at /releases/tag/<tag>.
Observe that the Pre-Release badge beside the wrapped title is cut off.
bugs.sourceCause: routers/web/repo/release.go SingleRelease renders the same repo/release/list template as the Releases list, so the details page inherits the list's shrinking status label in the title row.

relatedReference.name: Pre-Release status badge text is clipped on the mobile Releases page
relatedReference.distinction: Same badge clipping, but on a different page. That entry is the Releases list; this entry is a single release's details page at /releases/tag/<tag>.

bugs.name: Mobile tag row clips the Release details link for a tag with a published release
bugs.summary: At a 390×844 viewport, the Tags page row of a tag with a published release cuts its only action, Release details, down to "Release de". The visible part still opens the release.
bugs.expected: The tag row's Release details action is fully readable at narrow widths.
bugs.actual: For two freshly published releases, the Tags page row at 390×844 showed "Release de" at the right edge. Tapping the visible part opened the release. At 414 pixels and wider the full label shows.
reproSteps: Publish a release on a new tag.
Set the viewport to 390×844 CSS pixels.
Open the repository's Tags page and search for the tag.
Observe that the row's Release details link is cut off.
bugs.sourceCause: templates/repo/tag/list.tmpl renders tags in a "ui very basic striped fixed table single line" table, so the action cell can't wrap and clips its links at narrow widths.

relatedReference.distinction: Same Tags page and fixed single-line table, but a different row. That entry is a tag without a release, where New Release is clipped and Delete Tag can't be reached; this entry is a tag with a published release, where Release details is clipped but still tappable.
